title: Relative first cohomology and torsors with a specified open section
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion, and $j:V=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use the derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. A $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor] means a sheaf of sets with a $G$-action which is locally equivariantly isomorphic to $G$ acting on itself. Use derived global sections $R\Gamma$ and their cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and the mapping cone and shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put
$$H^q(T,V;G)=H^q\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,G)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(V,j^{-1}G))[-1]\bigr).$$
There is a canonical bijection between $H^1(T,V;G)$ and the isomorphism classes of pairs $(P,s)$ consisting of a $G$-torsor $P$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and a section $s\in(j^{-1}P)(V)$; isomorphisms must carry the specified section to the specified section. It sends the trivial torsor with its identity section to zero. The map $H^1(T,V;G)\to H^1(T,G)$ forgets $s$ and gives the ordinary torsor class. This bijection is natural under morphisms $G\to G'$ (contracted product of torsors [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]) and under morphisms of schemes $h:T'\to T$, with $V'=h^{-1}V$, followed by any coefficient morphism $h^{-1}G\to G'$.
For any short exact sequence $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$, the relative groups have the natural connecting maps $H^q(T,V;G_3)\to H^{q+1}(T,V;G_1)$; these commute with forgetting the specified support and with the preceding pullback and coefficient maps.

proof.text: For every supplied injective resolution I, use the explicit equivalence relativeTorsorEquiv between pointed torsor classes and actual relative cone homology [lem-amb-relative-cocycle-coordinates], and compose it with negation. This gives the simultaneous family e. The raw equivalence sends the trivial torsor with zero section to zero, and negation preserves zero.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; agent-written relative lifting-torsor refinement of its injective-resolution argument.

proof.text: Present an arbitrary torsor P as the lifting torsor of a global cycles section s. The presentation formula evaluates its raw relative class on this frame. By [lem-amb-relative-torsor-forget-normalization], forgetting the raw class gives −δ(s) under any supplied canonical comparison. Negation cancels this minus sign, while the absolute torsor theorem classH1_lifts identifies δ(s) with the class of P. This proves the specified forget compatibility without changing its signature.

proof.text: For a contracted-product presentation q, the map t↦q(t,0) is a natural f-equivariant torsor map, by quotient_natural, quotient_invariant and quotient_vadd. Apply the coefficient part of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-class-naturality] and the commuting restriction square relativeSectionMap_square. Homology maps preserve negation, so the result also holds for e.

proof.text: For the existing resolution-comparison declarations, direct image preserves injectives by its adjunction with exact inverse image. Recursively extend the degree-zero map and factor its differential through the next image, obtaining an augmentation-preserving comparison. The same recursion applied to a difference constructs comparison homotopies. Enough injectives supplies the target resolution where existence is requested.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; agent-written relative lifting-torsor refinement of its injective-resolution argument.

proof.text: Evaluate a comparison homotopy on terminal and open sections. MappingCone.mapHomotopy sends the commuting restriction-square homotopy to a cone homotopy, and shifting preserves it. The same argument after the section transfer proves independence of relativeTransfer on its resolution comparison. These are concrete homotopies of the given complexes, and require no bounded-derived descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; agent-written relative lifting-torsor refinement of its injective-resolution argument.

proof.text: For a short exact coefficient sequence, choose the existing compatible horseshoe resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]. Each degreewise row splits since its first object is injective. Section evaluation, extension by zero, biproducts in the cone and shifting preserve the split rows, giving the short exact relative complex sequence. Its connecting morphism is the Mathlib homology-sequence connecting morphism, and projection gives compatibility with forgetting. The diagonal cone-map formula is the single shared coneMap_XIso theorem from [lem-amb-relative-cocycle-coordinates].

proof.text: A supplied coefficient-sequence comparison or pullback-sequence comparison induces a morphism of the short exact relative complex sequences. The commuting squares follow from functoriality of relativeSectionMap and relativeTransfer. Apply HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.δ_naturality to prove the two existing boundary-naturality declarations.
